dates: Every opening year in this file is provisional. Research Bot is still confirming them. Parkway opening years stay provisional pending a check against KYTC's own document.

verification.title: Transportation map proof of concept: source verification
rules: Do not use KYTC GIS line data. It has no explicit license and may involve cost recovery.
Rail geometry is USDOT/BTS NTAD North American Rail Network Lines, public domain.

Parkway geometry is USDOT/BTS NTAD National Highway System, public domain. OpenStreetMap (ODbL, credited as (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, in a separate file) is the alternative when NTAD is not used.
Parkway opening years stay provisional pending a check against KYTC's own document.

filter: A line is drawn when opened <= year and (closed > year or the feature has no closed year). This extract has no closed years.
simplify: Douglas-Peucker at about 100 meters, then coordinates rounded to 4 decimal places. Gaps of 2 km or less between pieces of the same route were closed with a straight segment. Fragments shorter than 2 km that did not join were dropped.

frame.note: Already on the site. Used only as the map frame, not as transport geometry.

features.name: Lexington & Ohio Railroad
features.dateNote: Provisional. Research Bot is still confirming this date. The first segment is dated 1834–35; the line is drawn from 1835, when cars were running between Lexington and Frankfort.
features.summary: First railroad in Kentucky, Lexington to Frankfort. Opening year is provisional (1834–35).
features.selection: NTAD lines with RROWNER1 RJCC, DIVISION CENTRAL KY, and BRANCH OLD ROAD, kept where the segment midpoint is between longitude -84.905 and -84.488 and latitude 38.03 and 38.23. That is the Lexington–Frankfort alignment. Louisville Water Street leads, the line west of Frankfort, and the line east of Lexington are not included.

features.name: Louisville & Nashville main line
features.dateNote: Provisional. Research Bot is still confirming this date. The year is the through-line completion (first Louisville–Nashville train, 27 October 1859), not the earlier section openings.
features.summary: L&N main line from Louisville toward Nashville, drawn from the provisional 1859 completion.
features.selection: NTAD lines with RROWNER1 CSXT and SUBDIV MAIN LINE: the Louisville Division in Kentucky and the same subdivision’s continuation into Tennessee toward Nashville. Urban terminal track that NTAD files under other subdivisions is not included.

features.name: Cincinnati Southern to High Bridge
features.dateNote: Provisional. Research Bot is still confirming this date. Northern portion, Cincinnati through Lexington to High Bridge.
features.summary: Cincinnati Southern from Cincinnati through Lexington to High Bridge. Provisional opening 1877.
features.selection: NTAD lines with RROWNER1 NS and SUBDIV one of FIRST DISTRICT CNO&TP, SECOND DISTRICT CNO&TP, CNO&TP NORTH, or CNOTP NORTH, north of High Bridge.

features.name: High Bridge
features.dateNote: Provisional. Research Bot is still confirming this date. The point is the NTAD vertex nearest the Kentucky River crossing, 73 meters from 37.8167 N, 84.7214 W.
features.summary: High Bridge on the Cincinnati Southern, over the Kentucky River. Provisional opening 1877.
features.selection: Point snapped to the NTAD Cincinnati Southern centerline at the Kentucky River crossing. Rounded to 4 decimal places.

features.name: Cincinnati Southern south of High Bridge
features.dateNote: Provisional. Research Bot is still confirming this date. The year is the through route to Chattanooga, not each construction section.
features.summary: Cincinnati Southern south of High Bridge through Kentucky and into Tennessee. Provisional through-line year 1880.
features.selection: Same NTAD Cincinnati Southern subdivisions as the northern portion, south of High Bridge, including the NTAD continuation into Tennessee. The extract does not reach Chattanooga.

features.name: Western Kentucky Parkway
features.dateNote: Provisional. Research Bot is still confirming this date. Elizabethtown to near Eddyville opened in 1963; a short 1968 connection to I-24 is not split out. The year stays provisional pending a check against KYTC's own document (verification commit c4b56b3).
features.selection: NTAD National Highway System, STFIPS 21, LNAME Western Kentucky Pkwy.

features.name: Mountain Parkway
features.dateNote: Provisional. Research Bot is still confirming this date. The Winchester–Campton road is usually dated 1963; the Campton–Salyersville mileage in this extract uses the same provisional year. The year stays provisional pending a check against KYTC's own document (verification commit c4b56b3).
features.summary: Bert T. Combs Mountain Parkway. Provisional opening 1963.
features.selection: NTAD National Highway System, STFIPS 21, LNAME Bert T Combs Mountain Pkwy and Combs Mountain Pky. The later extension toward Prestonsburg is not in this extract.

features.summary: Bluegrass Parkway, Elizabethtown to Versailles. Provisional opening 1965.
features.selection: NTAD National Highway System, STFIPS 21, LNAME Blue Grass Pkwy.

features.selection: NTAD National Highway System, STFIPS 21, LNAME Purchase Pkwy.

features.name: Pennyrile Parkway
